Notice Regarding California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determinations
Pursuant to CEQA, a "project" is defined as a "whole action" subject to a public agency's discretionary funding or approval that has the potential to either (1) cause a direct physical change in the environment or (2) cause a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment. "Projects" include discretionary activity by a public agency, a private activity that receives any public funding, or activities that involve the public agency's issuance of a discretionary approval and is not statutorily or categorically exempt from CEQA. (Pub. Res. Code § 21065.) To the extent that matters listed in this Agenda are considered “projects” under CEQA, their appropriate CEQA determination will be listed below each recommendation. If no CEQA determination is listed, it has been determined that the action does not constitute a “project” under CEQA.
Viewing City Council Meetings
Members of the public may view the City Council meeting live on the City’s website https://www.azusaca.gov/1389/Watch-Meetings-Online, or on Channel 3 (Spectrum). Archived video of recorded meetings is also available on the City website. Your attendance at this public meeting may result in the recording and broadcast of your image and/or voice as previously described.
Procedures for Addressing the Council
The Council encourages interested people to address this legislative body by making public comments. Public comments may be made during designated agendized public comment periods and during public hearing items. Public comments are limited to five (5) minutes per speaker, unless a different time is announced by the Mayor/presiding Chair.
The Council encourages free expression of all points of view. To allow all persons the opportunity to speak, please keep your remarks brief. If others have already expressed your position, you may simply indicate that you agree with a previous speaker. If appropriate, a spokesperson may present the views of your entire group. State law generally prohibits the City Council from responding to or acting upon matters not listed on this agenda. Council rules prohibit clapping, booing, or shouts of approval or disagreement from the audience. Clapping, booing, shouting or other actions from the audience which, disturbs, impedes, or otherwise renders infeasible the meeting’s orderly conduct, who, after a request by the presiding officer, refuses to cease such behavior may be removed from the City Council chambers or remote participation platform.

  THE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
  REGULAR MEETING
  MONDAY, NOVEMBER 17, 2025

The City Council of the City of Azusa met in Closed and Regular session at Azusa Auditorium at 213 E.
Foothill Blvd., Azusa, CA 91702.

Mayor Gonzales called the meeting to order at 6:30 P.M.

ROLL CALL: Roll call was taken by City Clerk Cornejo.

PRESENT:  COUNCILMEMBERS: GONZALES, ALVAREZ, AVILA, MENDEZ, BOW
ABSENT:  COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE

ALSO PRESENT

Elected Officials: City Clerk Cornejo

Staff Members: City Manager Gonzalez, Interim City Attorney Casso, Chief of Police Wenrick.

PUBLIC COMMENT - None

CLOSED SESSION

The City Council recessed to Closed Session at 6:30 p.m. to discuss the following items.

Interim City Attorney Casso announced that he was recusing himself from Closed Session due to a conflict of
interest.

1. PUBLIC EMPLOYEE APPOINTMENT - Pursuant to California Government Code, Section 54957(b)(1).
  Title: City Attorney

REGULAR SESSION

Mayor Gonzales called the meeting to order at 7:31 P.M.

ROLL CALL: Roll call was taken by City Clerk Cornejo.

PRESENT: COUNCILMEMBERS:  GONZALES, ALVAREZ, AVILA, MENDEZ, BOW
ABSENT: COUNCILMEMBERS:  NONE

ALSO PRESENT

Elected Officials: City Clerk Cornejo

City Council Minutes  Page | 1
November 17, 2025
 Staff Members: City Manager Gonzalez, Interim City Attorney Casso, Deputy City Manager DeAnda-Scaia,
Chief of Police Wenrick, City Clerk Services Manager Juarez, Director of Economic and Community
Development Jimenez, Public Works Superintendent Chavez, Director of Community Resources Carpenter,
City Librarian Hassen, Director of I.T. Guadagnino, General Manager of Utilities Singh

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by AUSD Superintendent, Arturo Ortega.

The Invocation was led by Pastor Daniel Simonson, Christbridge Immanuel Church.

CLOSED SESSION

City Manager Gonzalez announced the following regarding closed session: The City Council heard a report and
provided direction to Staff; and no formal action was taken.

PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

Tony Martinez, Northstar Land Care Founder and President, addressed Item D-1 to express the Company’s
desire to be awarded the tree maintenance contract and stated the ways that the company would provide service
to the community.

Ernesto Macias, Tree Service Kings Vice President, addressed Item D-1 to express the Company’s desire to be
awarded the tree maintenance contract and provided information about rates and services.

Arturo Ortega, AUSD Superintendent, shared District highlights on behalf of the Board of Education.

John Pineda, West Coast Arborist Area Manager, provided information about the Company’s involvement with
the community.

Pat Mahoney, West Coast Arborist President and Owner, stated that the Company has provided service to the
City for the past 25 years; and highlighted the value brought to the City.

Diana Reyes Williams and Jeanette Fruta, members of the Azusa Woman’s Club, shared information about the
Azusa Woman’s Club and its history with the Azusa Library; asked that the Council and community save the
date of January 18, 2026 to mark the 125th anniversary; and announced upcoming events.

Jesus Soto discussed Ordinance 1-12 related to involuntary labor in relation to imprisoned individuals and
requested that the Council amend or strike the Ordinance from the record.

REPORTS, UPDATES, AND ANNOUNCEMENTS FROM STAFF/COUNCIL

“Pet of the Month” Presentation

Los Angeles County Animal Control Officer Rivas introduced an unnamed Shepard-Husky mixed 5-month old
puppy who was recently surrendered and is ready for adoption.

City Manager Communications

City Manager Gonzalez gave kudos to City Staff for the number of events being held by the City; and
announced the grand opening of Vallarta Supermarket on December 10 at 7:00 a.m.

He responded to questions posed by the Council in relation to the number of attendees at the Cruising Back 2
Route 66 car show, stating that Staff extimated 836 participant vehicles and 4,000 attendees.

City Clerk

City Clerk Cornejo stated that there were 11 applications received for the Commission vacancy; and inquired
about a possible date for the interviews.

It was the consensus of the Council to hold interviews on December 8 at 6:00 pm, at the Azusa Light & Water
Department.

City Council Minutes  Page | 2
November 17, 2025
 Councilmember Announcements

Mayor Pro Tem Alvarez commented on the successful car show; mentioned the ribbon cutting for the Old
School House, noting the amazing job that was done on the project; and shared the passing of Azusa
community member Nuno Romero and asked for prayers for the Romero family.

Councilmember Avila thanked staff for the successful events that have been taking place, including the
Veterans Day Ceremony and Banner Ceremony held over the weekend; and extended his condolences to the
Romero family.

Councilmember Mendez announced the Household and E-Waste Cleanup Collection held on November 29,
2025; noted the success of the Car Show; and expressed his gratitude for the preservation of the Old
Schoolhouse.

Councilmember Bow congratulated City staff on the plethora of events; highlighted City Clerk Cornejo’s
speech at the Old Schoolhouse ribbon-cutting ceremony; and announced Assemblymember Rubio’s annual
Operation Gobble, held on November 23.

Mayor Gonzales gave kudos to staff for the number of events put on; expressed his appreciation for City Clerk
Cornejo and the work he did on the Old Schoolhouse project; and requested an update on the Dog Park ribbon
cutting.

SCHEDULED ITEMS

CONSIDERATION TO AWARD A THREE-YEAR CITYWIDE TREE MAINTENANCE CONTRACT FOR
PARK, PARKWAYS, MEDIAN ISLANDS AND UTILITY RIGHT OF WAY TREES IN RESPONSE TO
THE CITY’S REQUEST FOR QUALIFICATIONS

Mayor Gonzales announced that he is recusing himself from the discussion of the Item due to the perception of
a conflict of interest.

Director of Public Works/City Engineer Delgadillo provided a history of the Request for Qualifications (RFQ)
process; gave an analysis of the proposals received; and discussed the proposed contract schedule.

At the request of the Council, Interim City Attorney Casso described the difference between a Request for
Proposals and a Request for Qualifications.

In response to questions posed by the Council, Director Delgadillo stated that the reason Staff did not include a
recommendation for the Council was to allow the Council to have an open discussion about the proposals
received; discussed qualifications needed; and explained that the discrepancy in the number of trees was an
oversight.

Roy Chavez, Public Works Superintendent, stated that there is currently one truck being utilized for the
trimming of palm trees; and detailed the types of special equipment described in the RFQ.

There was discussion regarding the desire to remain within budget when awarding the contract, the large gap in
the bid price of two of the bidders, the process for terminating a contract, the RFQ process, bids received, and
the various contractors.

There was further discussion regarding the selection of either West Coast Arborists, Inc. or Northstar Land
Care.

It was the consensus of the Council to continue the item to the December 1, 2025 meeting to allow the Council
the opportunity to further examine the proposals received.
